exposure: Calendar months with mean temperature above 20 degC
cohort: The study included 116,981 hip and knee arthroplasty procedures performed between January 2013 and September 2019 in 122 hospitals participating in Swiss SSI surveillance.
finding: Surgical site infection rates after hip and knee replacement increase with higher environmental temperature, with significantly higher rates observed for procedures performed in summertime or months with mean temperatures above 20 degC.
